title: DepEd: Lack of qualified applicants leaves 'hard-to-fill' posts vacant
summary: Aside from teaching positions that the Department of Education (DepEd) has yet to fill, the agency said some “hard-to-fill” posts remain vacant due to several factors, including a lack of qualified…

blocks.text: The Department of Education (DepEd) said some “hard-to-fill” positions in the agency remain vacant due to a lack of qualified applicants and other factors.

“The reasons behind the delays in filling up some of these plantilla positions are attributed to several factors. One of these is that there are hard-to-fill positions, which include the non-teaching positions,” House Committee on Appropriations Vice Chair and Davao De Oro Rep. Maria Carmen Zamora said on Tuesday.
Zamora made the statement while defending the department’s proposed 2027 budget during plenary debates in the House of Representatives.
According to Zamora, among these hard-to-fill positions are guidance counselors, attorneys, and special education and science teachers,

“There are also factors like waiving of beneficiaries under special hiring guidelines, and there are instances where there are a lack of qualified applicants for appropriate specializations,” she said.
Previously, during a House of Representatives budget deliberation on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget, the agency received zero allocation for the hiring of new teachers in the next fiscal year.

ACT Teachers Party-list Representative Antonio Tinio asked DepEd whether it would still refrain from requesting new plantilla items, given the agency’s previous report of a shortage of more than 14,000 teachers.
In response, Zamora explained that the department’s hiring process remains ongoing and will continue until December this year.

“The Department is on its continuous hiring process until next year, because the allocation given to the department from the GAA (General Appropriations Act) 2026 is still being implemented starting this year,” Zamora said.
“...Therefore, there’s no such thing that we stopped hiring. We are still hiring as we speak until December of this year,” she added.
Zamora said the 2026 GAA created a total of 31,428 positions, of which 22,711 had been filled and 8,688 remained vacant as of June 30, 2026.
The number of vacant teaching positions under DepEd currently stands at more than 20,000, factoring in an additional 12,646 unfilled positions carried over from previous years, according to Zamora.
Out-of-pocket expenses
The House on Tuesday approved the proposed P975.96-billion budget of DepEd for 2027.
Several lawmakers flagged decreases in allocations for some line items, including a minimal increase in the department’s Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE).
MOOE refers to funds allocated for the day-to-day operating expenses of the department, including individual public schools across the country.
Tinio pointed out that the minimal MOOE increase would be outpaced by the country’s inflation rate, providing little relief amid rising prices.
“Why is the proposed increase in the NEP and the General Appropriations Bill so small, not even reaching one percent?” Tinio said in Filipino.
“That means, in effect, this is a decrease because it is way below even the current inflation rate today. So, it did not even keep pace with it,” he added.

Tinio said the low MOOE allocation remains a primary complaint among schools, with teachers often forced to pay out of pocket for classroom and school needs.
“If we ask the schools, that is one of the basic complaints. At the school level, the MOOE is insufficient, right?” Tinio said.
“Generating operating expenses is always a problem, and it is often left to teachers to cover out of their own pockets,” he added.

For its part, Zamora said DepEd follows a formula in determining allocations for each school, adding that the department implemented a policy adjustment last year to refine these allocations based on various factors.
“In line with the setting of the formula in terms of allocation of MOOE for schools, we take note… Very valid observation,” Zamora said.
Tinio proposed that roughly P3 billion be added to the MOOE allocation to help schools keep pace with inflation. — MCG, GMA News
